_v1_notes.TRANSMISSION MODE|INTERVENTION: vector elimination is N for everything except mosquito-borne, since there is no vector to eliminate. Water treatment is N except for waterborne. Blood screening is N except for blood contact. Contact tracing is N for vector-borne and waterborne: neither has person-to-person chains to trace. Vaccination is plausible for all four.
_v1_notes.TRANSMISSION MODE|SETTING: respiratory in a refugee camp, urban, rural and closed institution are all plausible. Blood contact in a refugee camp is Y (unsafe injection) but N in a closed institution only if that institution has no medical function - here it is Y. Vector-borne in a closed institution is N: controlled entry and indoor confinement break the vector's access. Waterborne in a closed institution is Y via a single shared supply. Blood contact in dispersed rural is N: no formal transfusion system to carry it.
_v1_notes.TRANSMISSION MODE|TIMEFRAME: vector-borne in the first 72 hours is N: transmission bounded by a mosquito life cycle is not a 72-hour phenomenon.
_v1_notes.INTERVENTION|SETTING: contact tracing in a dense urban settlement is N (case counts overwhelm it) and in a refugee camp is N (transient population, no records). Vector elimination in a closed institution is N: no breeding habitat under controlled entry. Blood screening in a refugee camp is N: no formal donation system exists.
_v1_notes.INTERVENTION|TIMEFRAME: vaccination and vector elimination are both N in the first 72 hours and in weeks one to four for vaccination logistics; vector elimination needs a breeding cycle so it is N at both short horizons. Water treatment, tracing and screening all act within days.
_v1_notes.SETTING|TIMEFRAME: no setting is incompatible with any timeframe.
